findings.title: An accepted initial read can remain unobserved after foreground return
trace: Candidate load() accepts a current read using mayPublishRead, which checks the current epoch/read ID, lifetime, saving and cancellation but does not require a foreground surface. It then sets actualOpenReadOwner = requestEpoch.
beginActualOpenIfReady refuses an inactive surface without consuming actualOpenAttemptedMountID. Its only current call sites are mount() and load().
Current UIKit viewDidAppear calls mount and requests load. updateUIViewController only calls applyInterfaceDirection and render; render/observation is not an activation trigger for the new operation.

Current DocumentView didBecomeActive notification calls recordEditorDiagnostic and consumeMiniAppsResults only. The diagnostic records state only; the complete current MiniApps implementation has no mount/load call and an empty pending-result collection produces no native operation.

Therefore a still-mounted document whose initial accepted read finishes while its scene is inactive has no activation callback that revisits the unattempted actual open. Ordinary foreground return without a new view appearance or explicit load can leave it unrecorded.

findings.minimumCorrection: Route the existing real activation callback through the same guarded readiness function, retaining the current mount/attempt identity. Do not reset the token, trigger writes from every refresh, retry an already attempted intent, or change editor read/draft authority.
findings.meaningfulRegression: An accepted read with a mounted but inactive surface produces no open dispatch; activating that same surface produces exactly one operation with the original mounted owner; repeated activation and ordinary refresh do not add operations.

acceptedSourceBoundaries: Real connectOwnedSpace captures expectedNetworkID from the original owned embedded session before suspension. Native account/run binding acquisition occurs inside the original session lease; all failures propagate to the existing session drain and journal close path. There is no unsupported-capability or HTTP-status downgrade.

A single captured actor store is passed through the original workspace owner, Root, Library and cached document construction. Explicit optional defaults preserve injected caller compatibility and are not a fallback in the canonical App connect path.

New Home actions are explicit. Their UI availability is independent of canWrite; current READ and account/run/lease validation remain delegated to the real Host API. Outer hierarchy menus do not suppress the new action for a reader. Built-in, absent, empty and unsupported selections are not converted to a Page.

The original prepared Home/open intent is retained before commit. The lock-protected Sendable holder synchronously checks and retains acknowledgment ownership metadata before the Host callback returns, without an actor hop. Original store consumption/ledger remains authoritative; no automatic resend or durable-journal claim is added.

Home defer checks the request ID, while publication checks the epoch/lifetime/request. Revoke cancels and retains owned Home work for the original drain. Document metadata operations leave accepted editor content, canWrite, drafts, save and composition behavior unchanged outside the exact additions.

Cached reopening is coherent in the inspected source: unmount cancels and retains the predecessor task; a new mount gets a new token/read owner; the successor installs its task ID before awaiting the predecessor. The old task's ID-gated defer cannot erase the successor, and old epoch/mount guards refuse stale publication. Drain retains and awaits the owned tasks.

Both the shared acknowledgment holder and document source use the same SwiftUI compilation guard. New cross-actor calls use the existing Sendable Host types and actor API; synchronous locking occurs outside async methods. No further concrete compile-shape blocker was found by source inspection.

language.existingMechanism: All new strings use unchanged AnyUIErrorText.text(he,en), which branches on Locale.autoupdatingCurrent.
language.conclusion: The retained bounded source trace found no divergent production App-language owner. It does not establish equality of Foundation, SwiftUI and bundle languages in every runtime state; both mixed App/OS visual directions remain NOT_RUN.

apiAndRuntime.qualification: New bound-start source and coherent Native exports remain required. The current 8ac artifact and the bae source alone do not establish compile/runtime acceptance.

inspectionLimits: Exact fixed-file read transport errors and output truncation were retained as inspection-only; successful complete source bodies were rehashed. This review is not test, Apple, Native, mixed-language or visual acceptance. Interfaces owns subsequent source correction and test additions.
